title: KV-to-host spill + micro-adapter fallback with request-priority shedding for OOM recovery
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We continue to see transient OOM events in high-concurrency workloads where long-lived KV caches plus sustained continuous-batching push GPU residency past safe thresholds. Existing mitigations (aggressive eviction and model fallback) are effective but cause quality cliffs and repeated retries. This ticket proposes a coordinated, low-latency salvage path combining: 1) non-blocking KV shard spill-to-host with async rehydration; 2) lightweight GPU-land 'micro-adapters' (small quantized kernels / distilled micro-models) that can serve truncated continuations while the main model recovers; and 3) request-priority shedding and token-level admission control integrated into the batcher. The goal is graceful degradation (serve something useful with bounded latency) and smooth recovery without broad cancel/retry storms.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New spill path writes KV shards to host RAM in <10ms per shard and can restore asynchronously with a configurable concurrency cap. 2) Micro-adapter path can be invoked automatically when per-GPU free memory < threshold and finishes generation within 2x median latency for equivalent prompt length. 3) Admission controller reduces batch admission rate for lower-priority requests rather than failing them; priority mapping configurable per-tenant. 4) End-to-end tests show reduced OOM-induced request failures by >=60% on synthetic long-KV load while mean user-visible quality degradation <10% measured on eval prompts. 5) Observability: metrics for spill rate, rehydration latency, micro-adapter usages, and priority-shed ratio are emitted and dashboarded.
design_notes:
High-level components:
- KV shardizer: split per-session KV into multiple cache shards (~1-4 shards per session) so partial spill/rehydration is possible.
- Spill store: host-resident LRU with async flush; shards are compressed using lightweight quantized encoding (e.g., int8 delta) before writing to host to reduce host memory and bus usage.
- Rehydration worker pool: bounded concurrency to avoid thundering-herd; supports prioritized queueing so critical sessions rehydrate first.
- Micro-adapter family: tiny distilled transformer heads compiled with quantized kernels for CPU and small-GPU memory paths; API-compatible with main model for short continuations and deterministic 'short-mode' tokens.
- Admission controller: integrated into the continuous-batcher admission step; exposes per-request priority, token budget hints, and a fast decision path to allow accept/defer/serve-via-micro-adapter.
- Fallback flow: on low-memory condition, batcher attempts incremental steps: (a) trim batch window (early admission reject for low-priority), (b) mark certain sessions for shard-spill, (c) route some requests to micro-adapter.
- Telemetry: expose gauges and histograms for GPU free memory, spill latency, rehydration success rate, micro-adapter conversion ratio, and user-quality deltas.
implementation_plan:
Milestones:
- Spike (3d): prototype host-spill for KV shard; measure per-shard CPU + memcpy cost across instance types. (owner: Mateo)
- Prototype micro-adapter (5d): build a distilled 50M-200M parameter head for a 7B model family, compile quantized kernel and test route logic locally. (owner: Claire Zhang)
- Admission controller + batcher integration (4d): add priority metadata to requests and implement shedding decisions in admission path with unit tests. (owner: Mateo)
- End-to-end test harness (5d): synthetic workload generator to stress KV + batching and simulate multi-tenant mixes. (owner: SRE lead)
- Canary rollout (2 weeks): enable on a small Dedicated pool with observability and kill-switch. (owner: Release Eng)
- Post-canary tuning: thresholds, shard sizing, micro-adapter temperature to reduce hallucination artifacts.
Implementation details:
- Config flags: runtime.kv.spill.enabled, runtime.kv.spill.shard_size_bytes, runtime.kv.spill.compress=on/off, runtime.kv.rehydrate.concurrency, batcher.admission.priority_shed_ratio, microadapter.max_tokens, microadapter.model_family.
- Failure modes: spill write error -> immediate fallback to micro-adapter; rehydrate CPU backlog -> mark session as degraded and continue serving via micro-adapter with exponential backoff for rehydrate attempts.
- Safety: do not spill PII-sensitive sessions unless KMS flag permits (privacy policy). Ensure spill data never leaves host and is wiped after session TTL.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Latency vs quality: micro-adapters will yield lower quality for certain instruction styles; evaluate prompt-dependent regressions.
- Complexity: introduces host memory usage and CPU work which may impact co-located services on host; need careful capacity and SLO budgeting.
- Determinism/consistency: partial KV restores could produce token discontinuities. We mitigate by only rehydrating prefix shards first and running a light consistency check.
- Security: host spill adds attack surface; restrict to dedicated pools or VPCs unless security review approves.
- Hardware variance: PCIe bandwidth and NUMA placement will impact spill/rehydrate timings; must test on cloud instance types we offer to customers.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for shardization and (de)serialization.
- Load tests with synthetic sessions (varying sequence lengths and KV sizes) to measure spill/recover latencies and micro-adapter fallbacks.
- Backpressure test: inject slow rehydration worker to validate shedding logic doesn't cascade.
- Quality regression: run eval suite (50 prompt families) comparing main-model outputs vs micro-adapter outputs and measure ROUGE/BLEU/embedding-sim similarity.
- Chaos test: force OOM on GPU process and verify fallback path completes successfully and metrics are emitted.
observability:
New metrics (names):
- runtime.kv.spill.requests_total
- runtime.kv.spill.success_total
- runtime.kv.spill.latency_ms_bucket
- runtime.kv.rehydrate.queue_length
- runtime.kv.rehydrate.success_total
- runtime.microadapter.invocations_total
- runtime.batcher.priority_shed_ratio
- runtime.session.degraded_count
Dashboards: memory-resilience overview, per-GPU telemetry and per-tenant spill/fallback heatmap, SLO alerting on micro-adapter-rate > 25% for > 10m.
rollout_plan:
1) Internal dev cluster feature-flagged for team testing. 2) Canary on Dedicated pool with conservative thresholds and observability. 3) Expand to Dedicated public customers opting-in. 4) Gradual release to hosted runtime with opt-in (disabled for private deployments unless customer approves).
Kill switch: runtime.kv.spill.enabled=false and microadapter.routing=off.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha: Created ticket after incident review on 2026-03-08 where 3 Dedicated nodes experienced transient OOMs under long-chat workload. Proposed hybrid host-spill + micro-adapter salvage flow.
2026-03-11 - Mateo: Spike in progress. Initial host memcpy numbers look promising on c7a equivalents; PCIe copy dominates on older instance types. Will prototype shard serialization next.

2026-03-12 - Claire Zhang: Built a baseline 75M micro-adapter that completes small continuations at ~1.8x latency relative to main-model median and uses <400MB GPU ram. Need to evaluate generation quality on instruction-following prompts.
2026-03-13 - SRE: Added test harness scaffold for long-KV synthetic load. Observed that rehydration concurrency >8 on small hosts causes CPU saturation; will cap at 4 by default.

2026-03-14 - PM review (Jordan Myers): Prioritize canary on Dedicated customers with strict data residency; ensure KMS gating for spill persistence. Also requested cost analysis for host-memory overhead.
Follow-ups: - Add automated experiments to measure customer-facing quality loss and threshold tuning; - Security review ticket to be opened after MVP spike completes.
